basis: F16a §6 DoD item: 'the trigger-eligible job set is a seeded column' plus the D-16 requirement that the dispatch core have something to dispatch from day one. Four rows: the two Wave-1 collectors already built (F08's attention snapshot, F04's market-data poll), the market-data poll's own D-15 trigger target (the bounded X sampling window job), and F04's Substack collector — seeded disabled because no JobHandler is registered for it yet (`src/services/jobs/handlers/index.ts`'s own doc names it as the next registration to land).

jobs.notes: F16 §4.1b step 1: 'the only part of this loop that runs unconditionally, and it is free.' Never gated by budget. Also evaluates F06's price.regime spike method per security and, on a positive verdict, opens a bounded x.sampling_window through JobService.
F08's existing collector (services/attention/collector.ts). Free, keyless, flat poll.

jobs.displayName: X sampling window (D-15 triggered, not clock-driven)
jobs.notes: D-15 §4.1b: 'the trigger may never dispatch a job that was not registered as trigger-eligible.' This row exists so there is something eligible to dispatch into — it must never be picked up by the ordinary clock scan itself, hence `farFutureNextDueAt`. Seeded DISABLED, and no JobHandler is registered for this job_key: an enabled row with no handler is the exact failure `seeded-jobs-have-handlers.test.ts` now forbids, and it was previously kept safe only by two independent conditions both holding (every X read ceiling at zero under D-32, and the far-future next_due_at). X is the only per-unit-priced source in the stack, so requiring a deliberate enable — not merely a raised ceiling — before it can ever spend is the safer default. No behaviour changes today: trigger.ts checks the ceiling BEFORE looking this row up, so a fired trigger is still refused at the ceiling and still writes its CoverageGap; and if a raised ceiling ever reaches the lookup, that path records a gap too. Whoever raises the ceilings (D-32's named switch-on trigger) must register a handler AND flip this back to enabled, in one change.

Enabled in the same change that registered its JobHandler (services/jobs/handlers/substack.ts), which is the sequencing this row's previous note asked for: never enabled with no handler, which would surface as a loud, misleading 'no_handler_registered' failure every tick. This is the job that starts D-16's forward-only clock — Substack needs no API key and no approval, so it is the one axis that can collect while Reddit waits on MT-13. Scoring is deferred: F20's durable queue does not exist yet, so the handler passes deferredScoringQueue() and reports the would-be backlog as `pendingScoring` on each run. Evidence rows are written before any enqueue, so the backlog is reconstructible when the store lands (MEMORY.md B-31 §4).

jobs.displayName: ApeWisdom full-board capture (all stock filters, all pages)
jobs.notes: Captures the whole ApeWisdom board into attention_board_snapshot, distinct from attention.snapshot which writes the universe-scoped attention_snapshot series analytics read. Both run. Kept because under D-16 collection is forward-only with no backfill and ApeWisdom is free and keyless: a board row not captured today is gone permanently, while a captured row nobody computes over costs storage and nothing else. Does NOT change what the product computes over — promoting a ticker out of the raw board into the 100-symbol universe remains an owner decision under D-27/D-30.
